reasons: AI-filled values are not validated before they overwrite the fields.
AI failures are only logged to the console, so the user gets no message.
The AI request runs in the browser. Where its key comes from is not visible in this file and needs checking in the provider file.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads React, the icons, the shared types, the store, the button and input parts, the AI provider and the voice recording button.
sections.why: Gathers everything the form needs in one place.

sections.name: GoalModalProps
sections.title: Input type for the popup
sections.what: Declares what the popup needs: whether it is open, how to close it, and an optional goal to edit.
sections.why: Lets the same popup be reused for both creating and editing a goal.

sections.name: GoalModal (part 1)
sections.title: Form state and AI auto-fill
sections.what: Creates a stored value for each field, filled from the existing goal when editing or from defaults when creating. Draws nothing while closed. Runs the AI fill by sending the user's sentence to the provider and copying each returned value into its field, with fresh ids for milestones. Also adds a milestone to the list.
sections.why: Lets AI fill and milestone entry work on the same fields the user can edit.
sections.watch_out: The AI result is written straight into the fields, and any missing value clears what the user had typed before.

sections.name: GoalModal (part 2)
sections.title: Removing milestones and saving
sections.what: Removes a milestone from the list. On save, works out progress from the milestones marked done, then either updates the existing goal or adds a new one, and closes the popup. Also draws the header with the title and close button.
sections.why: Saving is where the form's values become real stored data.
sections.watch_out: This form never lets the user tick a milestone, so progress only moves when milestones were already marked done elsewhere.

sections.name: GoalModal (part 3)
sections.title: AI quick-add box and title
sections.what: Draws the AI box at the top, with a sentence input, a voice button, an Auto-Fill button and the success message, then the goal title field.
sections.why: Puts the plain-language option first, so the user can start by describing the goal.

sections.name: GoalModal (part 4)
sections.title: Horizon, category, date and text fields
sections.what: Draws the time horizon, category and target date controls, then the vision and why text areas.
sections.why: Shows the main goal fields in a compact layout.
sections.watch_out: The horizon and category options are fixed lists. A new value added to the types file must also be added here.

sections.name: GoalModal (part 5)
sections.title: Reward, milestones and buttons
sections.what: Draws the reward field, the milestone entry box with an Add button and a list with remove buttons. Ends with Cancel and Create or Update buttons, which submit the form.
sections.why: Finishes the form and connects the save button to the save logic.

summary: A popup form for creating or editing a goal, with an AI box that fills the fields from a plain-language sentence.
purpose: Lets the user enter every goal detail in one place, either by typing or by describing the goal in words.
why: One form serves both creating and editing, so the same fields and save rules apply in both cases.
how: Fills each field from the existing goal when editing, or from blank defaults when creating. If the user asks, sends the sentence to the AI parser and copies the answer into the fields. Lets the user add and remove milestones. On save, works out progress from the completed milestones, then either updates the goal or adds a new one, and closes the popup.
inputs: Whether the popup is open, a close function, and an optional existing goal. The typed fields, the AI sentence, and voice input from the voice button.
outputs: Calls the store to add or update a goal, then closes. Nothing else is shown except the form.
risks: AI output is copied into the fields with almost no checking, and missing values blank out what the user typed. A failed AI call shows no message to the user, only a console error. Saving with an empty title does nothing and gives no hint. Progress is calculated only at save time.
debug: If AI fill does nothing, check the browser console for the AI Goal parse error message and the GroqAIProvider setup in aiAssistantEngine. If saved progress looks wrong, count the milestones marked completed. If Save does nothing, check that the title is not blank.
